The present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No. 413/2021 dated 07.07.2021 registered at Police Station Maharajpura, District Gwalior for offences punishable under Sections 195, 294, 506,
34 of the Indian Penal Code, and FIR bearing Crime No. 324/2024 dated 01.06.2021 registered at Police Station Maharajpura, District Gwalior for offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 506,
120-B of the Indian Penal Code, and also for a direction to conduct a free and fair investigation.
2.

At the outset, learned counsel for the State raised an objection regarding the maintainability of the present petition, submitting that the petitioners have sought quashment of two separate FIRs by way of a single petition, which is not permissible in law.
Hence, the present petition is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed.

5. Accordingly, the present petition stands dismissed as withdrawn insofar as it relates to the quashment of FIR bearing Crime No. 413/2021, with liberty to the petitioners to file a separate petition to assail the said FIR in accordance with law.

6. In FIR bearing Crime No. 324/2024, the prosecution case is that the complainant, Smt. Mamta Tomar, purchased land bearing Survey Nos. 46, 47, 48, 49, 64, 65, 66 and 67, admeasuring 2.517 hectares, situated at Village Maharajpura, Sindh Pargana, District Gwalior, pursuant to an Agreement to Sell dated 04.12.2019, for which she paid a total consideration of Rs.2,30,00,000/- to the accused persons.

It is alleged that despite receiving the said amount and repeated requests by the complainant, the accused persons failed to execute the sale deed in her favour and, while the said agreement was still subsisting, dishonestly executed another agreement dated 08.03.2021 in respect of the same land in favour of Tilak Singh, Pushpendra Singh and Rajveer Singh by falsely representing that the property was free from any prior agreement.

It is further alleged that Jagat Singh and his brothers executed yet another agreement concerning 10 biswa of the same NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7892 3 MCRC-59441-2021 land, misrepresented the nature and possession of the land, and described the diverted land as agricultural land.

The complainant further alleges that Rakesh Singh Gurjar, who had acted as a mediator and witness in the earlier agreement and had received Rs.10,00,000/- as brokerage, was aware of the prior transaction but still participated in the subsequent agreement and allegedly demanded additional money while threatening to obstruct the transaction.

It is also alleged that the complainant paid an additional sum of Rs.9,00,000/- for facilitating execution of the sale deed; however, the accused persons deliberately avoided executing the sale deed and entered into subsequent agreements with third parties with the intention to cheat and misappropriate the complainant's money.
When the complainant confronted the accused persons regarding the subsequent agreement, they allegedly threatened her with dire consequences, including death.
On the basis of these allegations, the present FIR has been registered against the petitioners and other co-accused persons.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the agricultural land bearing Survey Nos. 46, 47,
48, 49, 64, 65, 66 and 67, admeasuring 2.517 hectares, situated at Village Maharajpura, Gird Tehsil Morar, District Gwalior, is jointly owned and possessed by the petitioners along with the other co-owners, namely Ramhet and Mahendra Singh.

It is submitted that the co-owners, including the petitioners, had entered into an agreement to sell dated 24.07.2015 with Shri Hariom Tomar,
husband of respondent No.2, for the sale of the said agricultural land at the rate of Rs.88,00,000/-
per bigha, pursuant to which an advance amount of Rs.51,00,000/- was paid to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7892 4 MCRC-59441-2021 the petitioners.
As per the terms of the agreement, the land was to be sold either directly to Hariom Tomar or to any third party as directed by him.

The agreement further stipulated that a second installment of Rs.51,00,000/- was to be paid on 24.11.2015 and the remaining sale consideration was to be paid on or before 24.09.2016, failing which the agreement would become void and lose its effect.

It is submitted that Sugandh Singh Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198187481/

8. It is further submitted that thereafter, on 05.10.2016, the petitioners again entered into another agreement to sell with Hariom Tomar in respect of the said land, wherein it was agreed that the entire sale consideration would be paid before 05.04.2017, failing which the contract would stand cancelled.
Under the said agreement, the petitioners received Rs.1,02,00,000/- on the date of execution and a further amount of Rs.30,00,000/- was agreed to be paid in three installments within fifteen days.

However, Hariom Tomar again failed to comply with the terms and conditions of the agreement by not paying the remaining amount within the stipulated time, and consequently the agreement also stood cancelled.
It is submitted that for the advance amount received, certain registered sale deeds were executed by the petitioners in favour of the parties as directed by Hariom Tomar.

9. It is further submitted that subsequently, on 06.09.2018, Hariom Tomar along with respondent No.2 Smt. Mamta Tomar entered into another agreement to sell with the petitioners in respect of agricultural land bearing NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7892 5 MCRC-59441-2021 Survey Nos. 47, 48, 49, 64, 65, 66, 46 and 67 admeasuring 1.965 hectares situated at Village Maharajpura, Gird Tehsil Morar, District Gwalior, at the rate of Rs.94,00,000/- per bigha.

As per the terms of the said agreement, 50% of the total sale consideration was to be paid within six months and in case the remaining amount was not paid within the stipulated time, the agreement would become void.
It is submitted that even after expiry of the stipulated period, neither the remaining consideration was paid nor the sale deed in respect of the entire land was executed.

However, for the advance amount paid, Hariom Tomar got portions of the land sold through the petitioners to different purchasers in the form of plots and sections rather than purchasing the land as a whole.
10.

It is further submitted that respondent No.2 thereafter entered into another agreement to sell dated 04.12.2019 with the petitioners in respect of the remaining land, wherein it was agreed that the land could be sold either as a whole or in plots and the transaction was to be completed by 05.08.2020.
Under the said agreement, 40-50% of the sale consideration was to be paid within four months; however, the remaining amount was never paid to the petitioners.

It is submitted that the land which was sold through the petitioners at the direction of Hariom Tomar and respondent No.2 was divided into various plots measuring approximately 20,250 square feet and sold on the pretext of an undeveloped colony without obtaining any permission from the Nagar Tatha Gram Nivesh Karyalaya or the Nagar Palika Nigam, Gwalior.

Since the petitioners' names continued to remain recorded in the revenue records, the authorities initiated action against them NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7892 6 MCRC-59441-2021 for development of an illegal colony.

It is submitted that despite the fact that a sum of approximately Rs.7,00,00,000/- remained unpaid and no permission for development of the colony was obtained by Hariom Tomar or respondent No.2,
no steps were taken by them for execution of the sale deed for the entire land.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the petitioners issued a legal notice dated 12.08.2020 to Hariom Tomar and respondent No.2 informing them about the illegal acts committed by them in developing a colony without requisite permission and also stating that since the terms of the agreements had not been complied with, the agreements to sell stood void.
Thereafter, a public notice regarding the nullity of the said agreements was published in a newspaper on 14.08.2020.

It is submitted that despite their own breaches and illegal acts, respondent No.2 lodged the impugned FIR dated 01.06.2021 alleging that the petitioners had committed fraud and threatened to kill her.
It is submitted that the allegations made in the FIR are false, baseless and malicious.
The petitioners had preferred an application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before this Hon'ble Court and were granted anticipatory bail.

12. It is further submitted that thereafter another FIR dated 07.07.2021 bearing Crime No.0413/2021 under Sections 195, 294, 506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code was lodged by respondent No.2 alleging that the petitioners had abused and threatened her in order to compel her to withdraw the earlier FIR.
It is submitted that the said FIR is also baseless and has been lodged only with a malicious intention to harass the petitioners.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7892 7 MCRC-59441-2021 13.

It is further submitted that the petitioners have also instituted a civil suit bearing No.363A/2020 before the Court of the IInd Civil Judge, Junior Division, Gwalior against respondent No.2 and Hariom Tomar.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the said suit, the learned Trial Court, by order dated 28.08.2021, granted a temporary injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with the possession of the petitioners over the land in question.

It is therefore submitted that the allegations made by respondent No.2 in the FIR claiming ownership of the land and accusing the petitioners of intimidation and fraud are contrary to the findings of the Civil Court and cannot be sustained.

The petitioners have also submitted representations to the authorities on 21.09.2021 stating that respondent No.2, owing to her political influence, is misusing the machinery of the police to falsely implicate the petitioners and pressurize them to part with their agricultural land.

14. It is submitted that the present matter is purely civil in nature arising out of contractual transactions and disputes relating to agreements to sell, which has been deliberately given a criminal colour by the complainant in order to abuse the process of law.
In view of the above circumstances, it is prayed that the present petition be allowed and the FIR bearing Crime No.324/2021 be quashed insofar as it relates to the present petitioners.

15. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the petition and submits that the present petition filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is devoid of merit and is liable to be dismissed.

It is contended that the FIR bearing Crime No.324/2024 has been registered on the basis of specific and detailed allegations made by the complainant NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:7892 8 MCRC-59441-2021 regarding cheating, criminal breach of trust,
conspiracy and criminal intimidation committed by the petitioners and other co-accused persons.

The allegations disclose that despite receiving a substantial amount of money from the complainant pursuant to the agreement to sell dated 04.12.2019, the petitioners intentionally failed to execute Sugandh Singh Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198187481/
4 the sale deed and dishonestly entered into subsequent agreements with third parties in respect of the same land, thereby prima facie attracting the ingredients of offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 506 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the defence raised by the petitioners regarding earlier agreements, alleged breach by the complainant and pendency of civil proceedings are matters of disputed facts which cannot be adjudicated in proceedings under Section 482 Cr.P.C. at this preliminary stage.

It is well settled that merely because a civil dispute may also arise from the same set of facts, the criminal proceedings cannot be quashed when the allegations in the FIR disclose the commission of cognizable offences.
Hence, the State prays that the present petition seeking quashment of FIR be dismissed.

16. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.
17.
The scope of interference by the High Court in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is well settled.

The inherent jurisdiction is to be exercised sparingly and with great caution, and only in cases where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint, even if taken at their face value, do not disclose the commission of any offence or where the continuation of criminal proceedings would amount to an abuse of the process of the court.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7892 9 MCRC-59441-2021 18.

In the celebrated judgment in State of Haryana vs. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has enumerated the categories of cases in which the power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. may be exercised for quashing of criminal proceedings.

entities.text: State of Haryana vs. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, it has also been consistently held that such power is not to be exercised where the allegations disclose the commission of a cognizable offence and the matter requires investigation or trial.

19. Similarly, in Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, (2021) 19 SCC 401, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has reiterated that the High Court should refrain from quashing FIRs at the threshold when the allegations disclose the commission of an offence.

entities.text: Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, (2021) 19 SCC 401
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been observed that the High Court, while exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C., should not embark upon an enquiry as to the reliability or genuineness of the allegations made in the FIR.

20. It is also well settled that merely because a dispute may have civil consequences or arise from a contractual relationship, the criminal proceedings cannot be quashed if the allegations disclose the ingredients of a criminal offence.

In Indian Oil Corporation vs. NEPC India Ltd., (2006) 6 SCC 736,
the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the existence of a civil dispute between the parties is not by itself a ground to quash criminal proceedings if the allegations constitute criminal offences.

entities.text: Indian Oil Corporation vs. NEPC India Ltd., (2006) 6 SCC 736
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
21. In the present case, the FIR specifically alleges that the complainant had paid a substantial amount pursuant to the agreement to sell dated 04.12.2019 and that despite receiving such amount,
the petitioners did NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7892 10 MCRC-59441-2021 not execute the sale deed and instead entered into subsequent agreements with other persons in respect of the same land.
The FIR further contains allegations regarding misrepresentation and criminal intimidation.

Whether the complainant had actually paid the entire consideration, whether the Sugandh Singh Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198187481/
5 agreements had become void due to breach of their terms, whether the petitioners had the intention to cheat from the inception, and whether the subsequent agreements were executed in violation of the earlier agreement are all questions of fact which cannot be adjudicated in proceedings under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
22.

entities.text: Sugandh Singh Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The defence sought to be raised by the petitioners regarding earlier agreements, cancellation of contracts, development of an illegal colony by the complainant, pendency of civil proceedings and the injunction order passed by the civil court involves disputed questions of fact which would require appreciation of evidence.
At this stage, this Court cannot undertake a meticulous examination of such disputed facts while exercising inherent jurisdiction.
23. This Court is of the considered view that the case does not fall within the exceptional categories laid down in Bhajan Lal (supra) warranting interference at this stage.
Interference in the present matter would amount to stifling a legitimate prosecution and would be contrary to the settled principles governing the exercise of inherent powers.
24. Accordingly, this Court finds no merit in the present petition.

The petition seeking quashment of FIR bearing Crime No. 324/2024 registered at Police Station Maharajpura, District Gwalior for offences punishable under NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7892 11 MCRC-59441-2021 Sections 406, 420, 506 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code is hereby dismissed.
25. It is, however, clarified that any observations made herein are only for the purpose of deciding the present petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and shall not influence the trial in any manner.
